questions.heading: SimpleMaxFlow Finds the Most a Network Can Carry From a Source to a Sink
questions.stem: SimpleMaxFlow reports a flow of 40 from s to t, and its minimum cut is the two arcs A->t (capacity 15) and B->t (capacity 25). Which change could raise the flow?

options.says: s->A is not in the cut, and every unit must still cross A->t or B->t, which stay at 40.

options.text: Widen the arc A->t, from 15 to 20
options.says: Right: the cut's capacity bounds the flow, and only an arc in the cut raises that bound.

options.text: Add an arc A->B, so flow at A can also reach B->t
options.says: A and B are both on the source side, so the new arc does not cross the cut.

options.text: Widen every arc out of s by 10 each
options.says: No arc out of s is in this cut, so the bound of 40 is unchanged.

questions.heading: SimpleMinCostFlow Ships Supplies to Demands at Least Cost, and the Supplies Must Balance
questions.stem: Two depots hold 50 and 30 units and two towns need 35 and 40. A program sets the supplies 50, 30, -35, -40 on SimpleMinCostFlow and calls solve(). What does it get?

options.text: OPTIMAL, with the 5 spare units kept at the depot whose routes cost more
options.says: solve() meets every supply exactly; the lesson's 80-against-70 network came back UNBALANCED.

options.text: INFEASIBLE, since no route in the network can take the 5 spare units
options.says: The status names the cause: the supplies do not sum to 0, whatever the routes.

options.text: UNBALANCED, since the supplies and demands do not add up to 0
options.says: Right: they sum to 5; add a shelf node taking 5, or use solve_max_flow_with_min_cost.

options.text: OPTIMAL, with the 5 spare units shared out over the two towns
options.says: A town's balance row is an equation; it cannot take more than its demand.

questions.heading: When Demand Cannot Be Met, solve_max_flow_with_min_cost Ships What It Can
questions.stem: A weekly job calls solve_max_flow_with_min_cost() on a network whose towns need 90 units in all. The status is OPTIMAL and optimal_cost() is 410. How does the job learn whether every town got its units?

options.text: It compares maximum_flow() with 90, since this call may ship less than the demand
options.says: Right: on the closed-route network this call returned OPTIMAL after shipping 60 of 80.

options.text: It needs no check, since this call reports INFEASIBLE when a town is short
options.says: It reported OPTIMAL with 60 of 80 shipped; solve() is the call that says INFEASIBLE.

options.text: It checks that optimal_cost() is not 0, since a short town makes the cost 0
options.says: The closed-route run shipped 60 of 80 at $259k: a shortfall still has a cost above 0, and only maximum_flow() tells.

options.text: It reads the status again, since OPTIMAL from this call means all 90 arrived
options.says: OPTIMAL here means the cheapest of the largest possible shipments, which may be under 90.
